newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky-premature to seek permanent China MFN.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky-premature to seek permanent China MFN.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative nominee Charlene Barshefsky said it would be premature to seek permanent Most Favored Nation trading status for China.

"I think it is in all likelihood premature to seek permanent MFN status for China, inasmuch as we're in the process now of negotiating with China for WTO (World Trade Organization) accession," she told the Senate Finance Committee.

"I believe strongly the United States should not take any action to disincentivize China from making the kinds of market access committments with respect to WTO acession that permanent MFN might provide," Barshefsky said.

However, she said the annual debate over whether to temporarily renew MFN status for China -- which lets its goods into the United States at the same low tariffs that most other countries enjoy -- was not good for relations.

"On the other hand, the administration is looking at the question of this yearly annual debate, which as you know is corrosive of the relationship in the longer term." Barshefsky said it was a matter that the administration wanted to give much thought to and work with the finance committee on it.
